Summary of work performed

Exploration
- Located the functions referenced in the issue: php_fgetcsv in ext/standard/file.c and zif_str_getcsv in ext/standard/string.c (str_getcsv calls php_fgetcsv with stream == NULL).
- Inspected ext/standard/file.c around the parsing loops and identified memcpy calls that used the expression (bptr - hunk_begin - 1) as the size argument and then advanced tptr by the same value. When bptr < hunk_begin this can evaluate to a negative value, which on some platforms/ASAN triggers negative-size-param in memcpy.
- Found three occurrences of the pattern in php_fgetcsv where memcpy(tptr, hunk_begin, bptr - hunk_begin - 1); tptr += (bptr - hunk_begin - 1); (each inside enclosure-handling code paths).

Analysis and chosen fix
- Root cause: the code computed the copy length as (bptr - hunk_begin - 1) without ensuring that the result is non-negative before passing it to memcpy (which expects a size_t). If bptr < hunk_begin the signed-to-unsigned conversion produces a huge size, or ASAN may flag negative-size-param when memcpy is intercepted.

Possible approaches considered:
1) Add explicit bounds checks before each memcpy to ensure the computed length is > 0 and only call memcpy when it is. This is minimal and keeps existing logic.
2) Rework the parsing logic to guarantee bptr >= hunk_begin at all call sites. This is more invasive and riskier.
3) Use safer helper that clamps lengths to 0 and avoids copying when negative. Similar to (1) but centralized.

I chose approach (1) because it is minimal, localized, easy to review, and avoids changing parsing semantics beyond eliminating invalid/mis-sized memcpy calls.

Implementation
- File modified: ext/standard/file.c
- Change made: replaced the three instances of
    memcpy(tptr, hunk_begin, bptr - hunk_begin - 1);
    tptr += (bptr - hunk_begin - 1);
  with a guarded copy that computes a signed ptrdiff_t length, checks that it is > 0, then converts to size_t and copies that many bytes. The replacement looks like (conceptually):
    ptrdiff_t copy_len = (ptrdiff_t)(bptr - hunk_begin - 1);
    if (copy_len > 0) {
        memcpy(tptr, hunk_begin, (size_t)copy_len);
        tptr += copy_len;
    }
  (and preserves the subsequent statement hunk_begin = bptr as before).
- This prevents passing a negative size to memcpy and avoids advancing tptr by a negative/incorrect amount.
- I made exactly three replacements in ext/standard/file.c at the three locations flagged by the earlier grep.

Verification
- I attempted to run the repository build (secb build) and the repro (secb repro) in the environment to validate the sanitizer error is resolved.
- The patch was applied successfully (3 occurrences replaced). However, the build failed in this environment during configure/build (configure cannot compute suffix of executables; environment limitations), so I could not complete the secb build and run secb repro here to observe runtime ASAN results.

What I expect after a successful build/test run
- The invalid memcpy calls that previously could receive a negative size are now guarded: when (bptr - hunk_begin - 1) <= 0, no memcpy is performed and no negative size is passed.
- The particular ASAN error (negative-size-param) reported in the issue should no longer be triggered by the same inputs that previously led to bptr < hunk_begin.

Notes and recommendations
- The fix is intentionally minimal and focuses only on preventing negative sizes to memcpy. It preserves the existing CSV parsing logic and only guards the copy operations.
- Please run the following locally/CI to verify the fix end-to-end:
  1) cd /src/php-src
  2) secb build --verbose
  3) secb repro
  The security test (secb repro) should no longer trigger the ASAN negative-size-param for php_fgetcsv.
- If any compiler warnings related to ptrdiff_t or implicit includes appear, ensure the toolchain provides the standard headers (stddef.h is typically available via stdlib.h/stdio.h includes in this file). If needed, include <stddef.h> explicitly at the top of ext/standard/file.c.

Patch note / diff (conceptual)
- Replaced three occurrences inside php_fgetcsv parsing code with a guarded copy using ptrdiff_t to compute copy_len and only call memcpy when copy_len > 0. The rest of the function is unchanged.

If you want, I can:
- Produce an exact unified diff/patch file you can apply and run in your environment.
- Try to adjust build configuration in the current environment if you want me to continue making CI-environment fixes (but that may touch unrelated build infra). 

Files changed
- ext/standard/file.c (3 guarded-copy replacements inside php_fgetcsv)

Limitations
- I could not run secb build / secb repro to completion here due to build/configure failures in this execution environment, so I could not observe the runtime ASAN output. The source-level fix directly addresses the negative-size usage.

If you'd like the exact unified diff/commit or for me to try alternative fixes (centralized helper or a different boundary check), tell me which you prefer and I will prepare it.
